requiredClarification.issue: 100 marks old work interrupted and never replays its ID, but process death can release the store/adapter owner while its child is still alive. A new operation after restart could then start a second CLI even though the old operation was not replayed. The draft's no-close→fail-closed rule should explicitly survive that restart boundary.
requiredClarification.minimalText: After an abnormal executor stop, new CLI admission remains closed until the previous local child is known closed/reaped, or an explicitly documented termination/reconciliation mechanism proves no old child can remain. If that cannot be established, retain an explicit unknown/fail-closed state; do not infer a free slot merely from100 interrupted status or a new Node owner.
requiredClarification.focused102Check: A fake child outlives the first executor; restart and attempt a new operation. It must not create a second child until the declared old-child closure/admission rule is satisfied. Checking only same-ID no resubmission is insufficient.
requiredClarification.scope: Clarifies the draft's existing global1/no-close/lifetime contract. It does not require a new account/service or actual model call.
requiredClarification.resolutionVerified: Re-read revised draft lines39/41. It now explicitly states that100 ownership release/interrupted does not prove old child death, requires verified OS lifetime ownership or durable lease/unknown-child isolation, blocks other-ID admission when closure is unproved, forbids PID-reuse-blind killing or clearing all user processes, and adds the restart-with-old-child-alive/unknown→new-operation invocation0 check. Clarification accepted; this verifies design text only, not implementation.
